production_auth_probe.side_effect: one pending unlinked OAuth state; normal cleanup of expired auth states may run

incident.cause: Full systemctl ExecStart rendering includes dynamic PID/start/stop fields; hashing the entire rendering falsely treated a restart as command configuration drift.
incident.effect: Initially restored both old files after the sole successful restart; the new process stayed healthy.
incident.correction: Compare static path/argv/ignore_errors and all unchanged unit/drop-in hashes; bind a one-off anonymous start probe to the new PID listener to distinguish v2; atomically resync the same approved files without another restart.

limitations: Five-scenario acceptance used exact deployed bytes in isolated loopback HTTP and temporary SQLite, not production fake OAuth injection
JS tests used production JS read back into an independent Windows Node VM tree; Linux has no Node
No real WeChat identity exchange, real phone/browser acceptance or live customer checkout was performed
One anonymous OAuth start probe created a pending unlinked state (TTL900); no state/verifier/URL stored; state expires and normal future start handles cleanup, not a claimed scheduled deletion
